attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post predicting GPT-4's properties.

semantics.note: Firm 'will remain' about GPT-4. The normalised wording keeps all three parts: pastiche, useful for brainstorming and drafts, not trustworthy general intelligence. There are no conditions or horizon to keep.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair. It treats 'pastiche' as rhetoric that can't be tested, and it reads 'not trustworthy general intelligence' as consequential reliability failures, without needing a ruling on what counts as AGI. Because the speaker gave no measure, the result depends on this reading.

evidence.note: HBS institute's dated 2023 summary of its own researchers' GPT-4 field experiment. It reports large gains on creativity and writing tasks and says the AI falls short on other tasks.

Peer-reviewed randomized experiment, run June 2023 and published before the evaluation date. It found benefits inside the frontier and inaccurate output that hurt performance outside it, which shows both parts of the claim.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated, but the contract's early-resolution rule is met by a dated GPT-4 evaluation (2023 experiment, published 2026). It shows real gains on ideation and writing tasks and also consequential reliability failures outside the frontier. No counterevidence shows dependable general performance. The 'pastiche' part is rhetoric and is not scored.
